label: copy phase, outputting 3rd or later original token (recall_idx >= 2)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and only from recall_idx 2 on (outputting the third original token or later). It is silent on all original-phase steps, the <DEL> step, and the first two copy steps (just 35 activations at recall_idx 1). The predicate catches essentially all activations (recall ~1.0, mass recall ~1.0), but the feature is on for only ~29% of the steps it covers. Firing rate rises with recall_idx (0.10 at idx 2, 0.50 at idx 5) and is high on the last steps of long sequences. The largest activations are at the final step of L=3 sequences, especially when the first token is q (e.g. q v t <DEL> q [v]). Which eligible steps fire depends on token content in a diffuse way: prev_tok q/g/e and out_tok c/g/j have only about 2-3x lift, and no simple token or position condition improved precision much (recall_idx>=3 gives F1 0.50 but drops mass recall to 0.90).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: q, g, e, 0, z, w; least: d, k, r, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: c, t, e, w, 0, y; least: p, b, h, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, phase=2, L=4 & t=6.
